##  · K5-debt-lift-bound — sched-debt-lift bound is one round (&lt;= N+2 slices), not &lt;= 2 slices

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Evidence: Test bound only; the rules and OWNER DECISION 6 are unchanged. With discrete passes, spinners cluster at f or f+step, so any nonzero lift loses the equal-pass tie and waits up to one round. The bound becomes &lt;= (runnable + 2) x SLICE in sched-debt-lift and model property (i); it stays decisive against R12UnnormalizedLift (about 100 rounds). The residual is stated in plan section 10, and the red team is told at checkpoint 2.

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `066a1400e276c1fc898d5d68e6376ee7` · 2026-09-24T19:40:06Z

> Found while implementing commit 1 (the model); the plan's number is wrong, the rule is fine.
> 
> Plan section 10 says sched-debt-lift asserts that S's first run is <= 2 x SLICE. The model's debt-lift property fails it under the correct additive rule (seed 6: S waited 13 slices, with N=13-16 spinners).
> 
> Why: with equal-weight spinners, passes cluster exactly at the floor f (those not yet run this round) or at f + one step (those that have). A lift of any size, even the tiny epsilon = W/w_users (about 1.4e4 pass units, against a spinner step of about 1e8), puts S at f + epsilon. S then loses the tie to every spinner still at exactly f and waits for them all: up to one round, N slices. A sibling entering with no lift lands exactly on f and wins the tie (wake-first). The red team's estimate of about 0.01 slice treated the passes as continuous.
> 
> Proposed correction (test bounds only; OWNER DECISION 6 and every rule unchanged):
> - The sched-debt-lift case and model property (i) assert that S's first run is <= (runnable budgets + 2) x SLICE, i.e. within one round.
> - The lift then decays: once the floor passes users.pass, later siblings enter exactly at the floor.
> - It still catches R12UnnormalizedLift decisively: users.pass becomes f + SLICE x STRIDE / 1, so S waits about 100 rounds (thousands of slices).
> - Residual, stated: a destroyed lineage can delay one sibling created under the same shared parent within the same round by at most one round.
> 
> I'm continuing with this bound provisionally in commit 1 and will change it if you rule otherwise.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `2da2913c2839a3b7343d9ce7beaf82f6` · 2026-09-24T19:40:18Z

> Approved: the bound becomes S's first run <= (runnable budgets + 2) x SLICE (within one round), for both sched-debt-lift and model property (i). Your analysis is right: with discrete passes, any lift above zero loses the tie to spinners still at f, and one round is the ordinary cost of not being a wake-first tie winner, not a debt effect. Keep the case decisive against R12UnnormalizedLift (record the observed wait under the mutation in the commit message), and state the residual in the plan file's section 10 and in the case's comment: a destroyed lineage can delay one sibling under the same shared parent by at most one round, decaying once the floor passes the parent's pass. No change to OWNER DECISION 6. Also tell the red team at checkpoint 2 that this bound changed, and why.
